questions.skill: Understand a function as a rule that assigns exactly one output to each input, with a domain and a range
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Does the relation {(-2, 4), (0, 1), (2, 4), (3, -1)} define y as a function of x? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup: Does the relation {(-2, 4), (0, 1), (2, 4), (3, -1)} define y as a function of x? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. Each input has exactly one output. (Two inputs may share the output 4.)
questions.grading_note: Form required: yes or no with a reason.

questions.skill: Understand a function as a rule that assigns exactly one output to each input, with a domain and a range
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Give the domain and the range of f(x) = x² + 1.
questions.prompt_markup: Give the domain and the range of f(x) = x² + 1.
questions.correct_answer: Domain: all real numbers. Range: y ≥ 1.
questions.grading_note: Form required: both the domain and the range. x² ≥ 0, so x² + 1 ≥ 1, and every value 1 or more is reached.

questions.skill: Decide whether a relation is a function

questions.prompt_markup: A table pairs x = 1, 2, 3, 2 with y = 4, 5, 6, 7. Is y a function of x? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: No. The input 2 has two outputs, 5 and 7.
questions.grading_note: Form required: yes or no with a reason.

questions.skill: Decide whether a relation is a function

questions.prompt_markup: Each button on a vending machine gives exactly one kind of snack. Is the snack a function of the button? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. Each input (button) gives exactly one output (snack).
questions.grading_note: Form required: yes or no with a reason.

questions.prompt_markup: Two different inputs of a function can have the same output.

sections.skill: Restrict a domain to make a function invertible

questions.skill: Restrict a domain to make a function invertible
questions.standard_level: Precalculus. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Precalculus, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Explain why f(x) = x², with all real numbers as its domain, has no inverse function.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why f(x) = x², with all real numbers as its domain, has no inverse function.
questions.correct_answer: f(2) = f(-2) = 4, so an inverse would have to send 4 to two different outputs.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation.

questions.skill: Restrict a domain to make a function invertible

questions.prompt: f(x) = (x - 1)². Restrict f to the largest interval that contains x = 3 on which f is one-to-one, and write the inverse.
questions.prompt_markup: f(x) = (x - 1)². Restrict f to the largest interval that contains x = 3 on which f is one-to-one, and write the inverse.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the interval and the inverse. On x ≥ 1, f is increasing, and solving x = (y - 1)² with y ≥ 1 gives y = 1 + √x.
